findings.evidenceJa: お前、まだ何も返しちゃいないだろ
findings.explanation: Hamada says Haruki has not yet repaid or given anything back to the company that trained him. This is not a judgment that Haruki has accomplished nothing; the debt-to-company motif is repeated at lines 49 and 52.
findings.japanese:
「これからだろ…
お前、まだ何も返しちゃいないだろ…」
findings.todokanai: "You have so much potential… You haven't accomplished anything yet, right…?"

findings.explanation: The source contains only a startled or choked exclamation. The English invents a fully articulated defensive reply.

findings.highlight: letter of resignation for your editor position
findings.evidenceJa: 編集長に辞表出したって
findings.explanation: Haruki submitted his resignation letter to the editor-in-chief. The English instead implies he is resigning from an editor position, changing the grammatical role of 編集長.
findings.japanese: 「編集長に辞表出したって…どういうことだよ」
findings.todokanai: "Submitting a letter of resignation for your editor position… why would you do that?"

findings.highlight: But you live alone, don't you?
findings.explanation: Hamada says Haruki is unmarried, making 'family circumstances' an odd resignation formula before asking about his parents. Living alone is a different fact.
findings.japanese:
「家庭の事情とか？
でもお前、独身だよな？
もしかして、親御さんが何か？」
findings.todokanai: "Family matters? But you live alone, don't you? Did you hear something from your parents?"

findings.highlight: skills I have learned from both seniors and juniors
findings.evidenceJa: 先輩から後輩に脈々と受け継がれてゆくスキル
findings.explanation: These are skills handed continuously down from seniors to juniors. The English instead has Haruki learning from both groups and erases the intergenerational transmission he is abandoning.
findings.japanese:
先輩から後輩に脈々と受け継がれてゆくスキル、人脈、
そして、絆。
findings.todokanai: The skills I have learned from both seniors and juniors, the connections, and the bonds I have formed.

findings.highlight: you're still a rookie around here
findings.evidenceJa: まだ会社的には全然赤字なんだぞ
findings.explanation: Hamada says the company is still deeply in the red on its investment in Haruki. Rookie status is only the context; the explicit financial loss and unpaid obligation disappear.
findings.japanese:
「いくらお前でも、まだ会社的には全然赤字なんだぞ？
なんの恩返しもできてないんだぞ？」
findings.todokanai: "Even as you are now, you're still a rookie around here. You haven't given back anything yet!"

findings.highlight: not in a way that took too much initiative from yourself
findings.evidenceJa: 決して個人主義ってんじゃなくて
findings.explanation: Although Haruki sometimes charges ahead alone, Hamada says he is never an individualist. The English is nonsensical and does not preserve the distinction between solitary initiative and selfish individualism.
findings.japanese:
「たまに一人で突っ走ることもあるけど、
決して個人主義ってんじゃなくて、
何より、仕事と真剣に向き合ってた」
findings.todokanai: "There were times you did too much on your own, but not in a way that took too much initiative from yourself. Rather, you were very serious about your job."

findings.highlight: I'm supposed to get the boot
findings.evidenceJa: 俺が飛ばされんのが先だろ
findings.explanation: Matsuoka jokes that he should be transferred or banished to an undesirable post before Haruki disappears. 飛ばされる does not mean being fired outright.
findings.japanese:
「な………んだよそれ。
なんでお前が先にいなくなるんだよ？
どう考えても俺が飛ばされんのが先だろ！」
findings.todokanai: "What… the hell is this? Why are you leaving before me? Shouldn't it be a given that I'm supposed to get the boot before you do!?"

findings.explanation: Youko calls the situation the worst: it is Kazusa's desired result but not Youko's desired ending. 'Unfortunate' substantially softens her categorical moral judgment.
findings.japanese:
「けれど…最悪ね。
あの子の望んだ結果だけど、
わたしの望んだ結末とは違う」
findings.todokanai: "But… it's unfortunate. The resolution she wished for is different from mine."

findings.highlight: I would accept any divine punishment awaiting me. However, I couldn't bear seeing that happening to my daughter.
findings.evidenceJa: 天罰も地獄行きも覚悟してる。…けれど、我が娘が地獄に落ちるのは見るに忍びない
findings.explanation: Youko is prepared both for divine punishment and to go to hell herself, but cannot bear watching her daughter fall into hell. The English drops hell from both halves and reduces the daughter's fate to vague 'that happening.'
findings.japanese:
「わたしが直接壊したなら、天罰も地獄行きも覚悟してる。
…けれど、我が娘が地獄に落ちるのは見るに忍びない」
findings.todokanai: "Had I been the one directly responsible, I would accept any divine punishment awaiting me. However, I couldn't bear seeing that happening to my daughter."

findings.highlight: You won't be any less free than in Japan. No, I'll make sure you have even more freedom.
findings.evidenceJa: あなたに不自由はさせません
findings.explanation: Haruki promises Youko will want for nothing and suffer no inconvenience or lack in his care abroad. 不自由 here is not political or personal freedom, much less a promise of greater freedom than Japan.
findings.japanese:
「あなたのケアについては、俺が絶対に何とかします。
日本じゃなくても…ううん、日本以上に、
あなたに不自由はさせません」
findings.todokanai: "I'll make sure your medical needs are looked after. You won't be any less free than in Japan. No, I'll make sure you have even more freedom."

findings.highlight: the three of us will bear it all together
findings.evidenceJa: 二人…いや、三人だって抱えてみせます
findings.explanation: Haruki vows that he himself will support/carry two people—no, all three lives including Youko. The English redistributes the burden equally among the three, undoing Youko's warning that no one will support him.
findings.japanese:
「ちゃんと現地で仕事を探して、言葉も勉強して、
二人…いや、三人だって抱えてみせます」
findings.todokanai: "I'll make sure to find employment over there, I'll learn the necessary language, and the two of us… no, the three of us will bear it all together."

findings.highlight: Even though I have been adamant about this since the beginning, she has diverted the thread of the conversation to the bitter end.
findings.evidenceJa: 今まで散々煽っておきながら、最後の最後に梯子を外されてしまったことに対して
findings.explanation: Youko had repeatedly egged Haruki on, only to pull the ladder out from under him at the very end; his bravado may be retaliation for that. The English makes Haruki the previously adamant one and reduces Youko's reversal to conversation drift.
findings.japanese:
今まで散々煽っておきながら、
最後の最後に梯子を外されてしまったことに対して、
意趣返しをしたかっただけかもしれなかった。
findings.todokanai: Even though I have been adamant about this since the beginning, she has diverted the thread of the conversation to the bitter end. This is my tiny form of revenge for that.

findings.highlight: While the fact was obvious to Kazusa, I was unable to hide my shock
findings.evidenceJa: かずさは当然として、俺も、ショックを隠しきれていなかった
findings.explanation: Kazusa naturally cannot hide her shock, and neither can Haruki. The English turns Kazusa's visible shock into the verdict being obvious to her and leaves the emotion only with Haruki.
findings.japanese:
かずさは当然として、
俺も、ショックを隠しきれていなかった。
findings.todokanai: While the fact was obvious to Kazusa, I was unable to hide my shock when I learned her verdict.

findings.highlight: isn't feeling very well right now
findings.evidenceJa: 今はちょっと気弱になってるだけ
findings.explanation: Haruki argues that Youko is merely feeling timid, vulnerable, or fainthearted now and may think differently when her spirits recover. The English makes this her physical illness, obscuring his denial of her stated resolve.
findings.japanese:
「曜子さん、今はちょっと気弱になってるだけだって。
もっと元気になれば考え方も変わってくるって」
findings.todokanai: "Youko-san isn't feeling very well right now, but her point of view might change when she feels better."

findings.highlight: Then Kazusa won't be there during her final moments
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女の最期に立ち会えないことも
findings.explanation: Haruki fears that Kazusa might be unable to attend Youko's final moments. The English converts the feared possibility into a certainty.
findings.japanese:
もしかしたらかずさは、
彼女の最期に立ち会えないことも…
findings.todokanai: Then Kazusa won't be there during her final moments…

findings.highlight: that possibility is too cruel to even come to her mind
findings.evidenceJa: 敢えて思いつかないかのように振舞う
findings.explanation: Kazusa deliberately behaves as though she has not thought of that worst possibility. The English says it genuinely cannot enter her mind, erasing her conscious performance of denial.
findings.japanese:
けれどかずさは、その最悪の想像を
敢えて思いつかないかのように振舞う。
findings.todokanai: Yet to Kazusa, that possibility is too cruel to even come to her mind.

findings.highlight: you were the one who made me swear that stupid oath
findings.evidenceJa: そもそも勝手に誓いを立ててるのはお前だ
findings.explanation: Kazusa tells Haruki that he is the one arbitrarily imposing the vow on himself. The English says he made Kazusa swear it and adds that the oath is stupid.
findings.japanese:
「それこそ心配したって仕方ないだろ。
お前の意志がそんなに弱いわけがないし、
そもそも勝手に誓いを立ててるのはお前だ」
findings.todokanai: "Even less reason to worry then. You're not that weak-willed, and you were the one who made me swear that stupid oath in the first place."

findings.evidenceJa: 愛を育むことなんか、できるわけが
findings.explanation: Haruki says they cannot nurture or cultivate their love in the same place as Setsuna. 'Consummate' narrows this to sex, especially damaging here because the couple is explicitly discussing a promise not to sleep together.
findings.japanese: 愛を育むことなんか、できるわけが…
